description: MITHRIL is a team of two passionate innovators exploring science, technology, and discovery. We built DIVERGE, an AI-assisted scientific platform that uses real NASA data to investigate how Earth is changing. It analyzes temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, and solar radiation to identify long-term trends, detect unusual patterns, and explore relationships between environmental variables, turning complex data into meaningful scientific insights.
summary:
DIVERGE is an Earth science platform that helps people discover environmental patterns that might otherwise go unnoticed. It compares the same climate variables across different locations to identify places experiencing significantly opposite trends, such as one region getting warmer while another is getting cooler.

Using historical NASA data, DIVERGE analyses temperature and rainfall patterns, measures long-term changes, and helps users explore possible relationships between climate and the environment. We are also expanding it to incorporate satellite observations of vegetation, land-surface temperature, rainfall and land-cover changes.

The goal is to make Earth science more interactive and accessible, allowing users to explore real data, question patterns and investigate what might be happening in different parts of our planet. DIVERGE turns environmental data into opportunities for scientific discovery.
details:
About DIVERGE — Opposite Earth Discovery

DIVERGE is an Earth science platform designed to help people discover environmental patterns that are not always obvious when looking at the planet as a whole. Its main idea is simple: two places can experience completely different changes in the same environmental variable. For example, while temperatures may be increasing in one region, they could be decreasing in another. DIVERGE searches for these contrasting trends and helps users investigate why they might be happening.

The platform works by collecting historical climate data from NASA POWER for selected locations and time periods. It analyses variables such as temperature and precipitation, measures how they change over time, and uses statistical methods to identify significant trends. It then compares locations to find cases where the same variable follows opposite directions. An AI-powered explanation feature also helps users understand the findings, interpret the evidence and explore possible research questions without confusing correlation with causation.

One thing that makes DIVERGE different is that it does not simply display climate information; it actively searches for interesting patterns. We are also working to expand its analysis through additional sources, including ERA5, NASA GPM IMERG, MODIS, Sentinel-2, Landsat and Microsoft Planetary Computer. These integrations are intended to help connect climate trends with rainfall, vegetation, surface temperature and land-cover observations. Some of these data connections are still being tested and validated.

We developed DIVERGE using AppDeploy for application development and hosting, with React for the user interface, TypeScript for application logic, Vite for the development and build process, and CSS and Tailwind CSS for styling. We also used Lucide React for interface icons and Google Fonts, including DM Sans, Manrope and DM Mono, for typography. ChatGPT assisted us with brainstorming, research, coding, debugging, data interpretation and writing throughout development. We used python-pptx to generate our project demonstration presentation. NASA POWER provides the main historical climate data, while Microsoft Planetary Computer and other public data services form part of our multi-source expansion. DIVERGE is a web-based project and does not require specialised hardware.

Our creativity comes from approaching climate research through the idea of opposite trends. Rather than only asking whether the Earth is getting warmer or conditions are changing, we ask where, how and why different places may be changing differently. During development, we considered data quality, statistical significance, missing observations, different geographical scales and the importance of not presenting possible explanations as proven facts.

Our intended impact is to make environmental research more accessible and encourage people, especially students and young researchers, to explore real Earth data, think critically and discover questions worth investigating. We hope DIVERGE can help turn complex environmental information into meaningful scientific exploration.
